kurz: The AMW sends a short message to your phone when something is waiting for you – a question, an approval, a halt. ntfy is the simplest way: a free app and a secret channel name.
brauchst: The AMW runs on this PC (the service is set up).
The **ntfy** app on your phone (Google Play, F-Droid or App Store).

schritte.text: Run the command `amw push ntfy` on the PC. The AMW creates a random, secret channel name, shows it and stores it – afterwards it is listed under Settings › phone notifications as the channel (topic).
In the app tap “+”, enter the channel name exactly and subscribe. The server stays `ntfy.sh` unless you run your own.
So that tapping a message opens the right page: under Settings › Online site, enter the “Address of the online page” (`https://…`). As a command: `amw push link https://your-page.example/`.
Switch on the main switch and ntfy, save and press the test button for ntfy. As commands: `amw push an`, then `amw push probe ntfy`. The test arrives within a few seconds.

danach: The channel name is like a password: whoever knows it can read along. That is why messages only say that something is waiting – no content.
Quiet hours and what gets reported are set in the same place.
fragen: Can I use my own ntfy server?
Yes. Enter its address under “Server” and subscribe to the channel on that server in the app.
Yes, via Pushover or Telegram – both sit next to it in the settings.
How do I set up Telegram?

In Telegram create a bot with @BotFather and copy its token. Send the new bot a message. Then run `amw push telegram --token <token>` on the PC: the AMW shows the chat ID from your message. `amw push telegram --token <token> --chat <ID>` stores both.
How do I choose my own topic name?
`amw push ntfy --kanal <name>` sets your own name; without `--kanal` the AMW creates a random one.
